answer: An agent marketplace requires each active identity to lock $100 for 30 days before bidding on jobs, whether the task is to identify a bird by its plume, map a dune, or plan a voyage. Creating 10,000 fake agents therefore ties up $1 million. Splitting one deposit among many names does not qualify them: each must meet the same threshold. The defense makes a swarm costly through locked capital and lost access to that money.
